dialogue.text: Good morning, I'm Dr. Agent. Just so you know, I'm an AI assistant and this call is recorded for quality. I understand you've been experiencing episodes of unresponsiveness with facial grimacing — can you tell me when these episodes first started?
Good morning, Doctor. These episodes started about a month ago. I've had several of them, and they each last around 3 to 4 minutes.
Thank you for that detail — a month of episodes lasting 3 to 4 minutes each is important. During these episodes, are you aware of what's happening around you, or do you lose consciousness completely?
I don't remember anything that happens during the episodes. My family says I just stare and make faces, but I can't hear them or respond when they try to talk to me.

That's very helpful information — complete loss of awareness during the episodes is significant. Did you experience any warning signs or unusual sensations just before an episode starts, like a strange smell, taste, or feeling in your body?

Yes, actually! Right before an episode starts, I get this weird muddy taste in my mouth. It's really strange and unpleasant, and then the next thing I know, the episode is over and I don't remember what happened.

That muddy taste is a very important clue — we call that an aura, and it suggests the episodes are originating in a specific part of your brain. Have you noticed if your body moves in any particular way during these episodes, like jerking, stiffening, or twitching?
My brother saw me during one episode when I was waking up, and he said I was staring and making hand gestures with my hands. I don't remember doing that at all, but that's what he told me.
Those hand gestures during the episode are quite telling — that's focal motor activity. Have you had any head injuries, high fevers, or brain infections in the past that you're aware of?
No, I haven't had any head injuries or brain infections that I know of. I don't remember having any really high fevers either.
That's good to know — no significant prior head trauma or infections. Have you noticed if these episodes happen at any particular time of day, or do they seem to occur randomly throughout your day?
They seem to happen randomly — I haven't noticed a specific time of day. Some have happened during the day at school, and my brother saw one when I was waking up in the morning.

Okay, thank you for that information. Let me request some tests to help confirm what we're dealing with — I'd like to get an EEG to record your brain activity, and an MRI to look at the structure of your brain.

REQUEST TEST: EEG
REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI

- Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

**MRI Brain:**
- No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.

Given your aura of a muddy taste, the focal hand movements, complete loss of awareness, and these test results, I have enough to make a diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Focal Seizure Disorder with Temporal Lobe Origin (Temporal Lobe Epilepsy)
